title: Resource, Capacity, Constraint and Scarcity
results: Resource, Capacity, Availability, Allocation and Reservation are distinct.
Capacity may be physical, contractual or provider-defined and must name resource, scope, units and interval/model.
Availability is consumer/time-relative current usability rather than a future guarantee.
Entitlement, quota and limit do not imply physical reservation.
Linux cgroup limit overcommit proves configured limits are not reserved capacity.
Current ExecutionBudget is a committed per-Attempt physical-consumption ceiling vector rather than physical reservation.
MemoryMax, TasksMax and CPUQuota govern distinct resource dimensions and do not reserve memory/CPU/process capacity.
Windows native resource controls implement corresponding requested dimensions under target-specific accounting.
Time and retained-output limits are mechanical bounds but differ from machine resource capacity inventory.
Current global_limit is configured Runtime admission capacity rather than host machine capacity.
Current concurrency_reservations are genuine durable discrete-capacity reservations committed before physical dispatch.
held_orphaned intentionally preserves admission capacity under unresolved execution truth.
Current per-Workspace concurrency is a cardinality-one coordination capacity rather than hardware capacity.
Scarcity may be physical, contractual or policy-created and contention can exist before hard exhaustion.
Pressure is measured stall/degradation from scarcity/contention and is distinct from utilization.
CPU, memory, storage, network, locks, GPU memory, rate tokens and time have different resource semantics.
Overcommit can be valid; its safety depends on enforcement, reclaim, pressure and failure semantics.
Admission-capacity exhaustion is pre-commit and distinct from post-admission resource exhaustion.
Resource accounting, limiting, reservation/admission, scheduling and general resource management are separate responsibilities.
Current Runtime constrains/reserves selected resource dimensions but is neither an internal scheduler nor complete resource manager.
Dynamic pressure admission, multi-resource packing, priority and fairness remain unjustified without concrete fixed-capacity falsifiers.

nextRound.title: Scheduling, Coordination, Admission and Backpressure
nextRound.entryQuestion: Given eligible concurrent work and scarce capacity, who decides whether work is admitted, waits, is ordered, dispatched, rejected or backpressured, and which semantics belong to Runtime versus an upper owner?

notes: RF8 explains current budgets/reservations/capacity semantics but does not authorize scheduler, queue, PSI control, GPU allocation, priority/fairness or dynamic admission changes.
